Subject: Private deployment: operator scope, license carveouts and audit protocol (MSA / Order Form sync)

Hi all,

Thanks again for taking time to run through the deployment model yesterday. We captured a few follow-ups internally and wanted to align on a tight path to get the MSA + Order Form over the finish line for Acme's on-prem / VPC deployment. High-level asks from your side that I heard: operator access limitations, retention/audit windows, and proof-of-access for contingency.

To make this concrete we propose the following packet for legal review and procurement: 
- Clean MSA redlines (we attached v3) focusing on: operator access boundary, license run-time locality, and rollback/rollback evidence obligations;
- A short operator-runbook draft that describes technician access patterns and witnessing options;
- Order Form proposed changes to reflect dedicated capacity and retention SLA.

Questions we need answers to from Acme Legal / Procurement so Redwood can prepare final redlines:
1) Do you require operator witness or is remote verification of snapshot hashes acceptable?
2) Any minimum duration for evidence retention beyond the 12 months in the draft?
3) Are there procurement constraints (PO terms or insurance) that would affect our MSA exhibits?

Attachments: MSA_redlines_v3.pdf (redline), operator-runbook-draft.txt, order-form-proposed-changes.xlsx

If helpful, Aditya and I can be on a short call to walk through the redlines — propose Tue 09/28 14:00 ET.

Thanks,

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: legal@acmehealth.com
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@jarvissys.com
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 17:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private deployment: operator scope, license carveouts and audit protocol (MSA / Order Form sync)

Vanessa —

Appreciate the packet and the clear asks. Quick responses to your three items while our counsel reviews the attached MSA: 
1) For Acme, witness is preferred for any on-site keying or snapshot handover; remote verification of snapshot hashes is acceptable for periodic audits but not for initial handover unless an accredited third party is present.
2) We typically require 24 months of retention for forensic artifacts tied to production workloads; can you confirm Redwood's ability to provide that as an exception?
3) Procurement will need a standard PO and our ISV checklist filled out — I’ve included procurement@jarvissys.com. They will send a template and insurance limits.

Also please confirm whether operator console access is read-only for our admins or if operator sessions can escalate (we need the specific privilege matrix).

— Rebecca Park
Sr. Counsel, Acme Health
legal@acmehealth.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Rebecca Park <legal@acmehealth.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 26 Sep 2026 09:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private deployment: operator scope, license carveouts and audit protocol (MSA / Order Form sync)

Rebecca — thanks for the fast reply. A few technical clarifications from Redwood's side to help counsel: 

Operator access model (summary):
- Normal ops: operator sessions are limited to a dedicated support console with role-based views; no direct access to customer data stores unless a customer initiates a temporary support window.
- Escalation: for troubleshooting that requires deeper access, we require a two-party process: (a) customer approval + timeboxed access token, and (b) audit logging and snapshot of the session preserved.
- Witnessing: we can support on-site witnessing or a third-party witness (mutually agreed auditor). Our runbook draft lists the steps and hash verification flow.

Retention: we can commit to 24 months retention for forensic artifacts related to the Acme environment as long as it is captured in the Order Form exhibit (we will include storage cost assumptions in the order form).

Privilege matrix: attached in the runbook (operator-runbook-draft.txt) — high level: read-only console for account admins; support engineers have escalated troubleshooting roles that are auditable and timeboxed.

I also attached MSA_redlines_v3.pdf with comments inline — major legal items are marked with COMMENT: [redwood:ops-access] or [redwood:retention].

We’re open to the call on Tue 09/28 14:00 ET — Vanessa and I can host.

Thanks,

Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Hi Vanessa / Aditya —

Procurement here. A couple of practical items before we can route the PO: 
- Insurance: our minimum is $5M GL and we need Redwood's certificate and any SSH key custody endorsements.
- Billing cadence: Acme prefers net-60; is that acceptable or do you require net-30 for reserved capacity?
- Invoice remit: please confirm if Redwood accepts ACH to account ending -4321 and provide billing contact.

Also, regarding the 24-month retention commitment — we need the cost line item on the Order Form (line 7) spelled out as "forensic artifact retention (24 months)". If Redwood can confirm the pricing we can insert it in the PO template.

Thanks,

David Lin
Senior Procurement Manager
Jarvis Systems (on behalf of Acme Health)
procurement@jarvissys.com

Team —

Thanks for the clarifications — quick summary and proposed next steps so nothing falls through the cracks: 
1) Witnessing: Acme prefers on-site witness for handover; Redwood will offer on-site or third-party witness. Aditya will enumerate witness options and costs in the runbook. (Action: Aditya — update runbook by EOD Wed 09/29)
2) Retention: Redwood confirms 24 months for forensic artifacts as an Order Form line item. (Action: Vanessa / Sean — add the line to Order Form and include the cost estimate)
3) Privilege matrix: Aditya attached the matrix; legal to confirm if the language in MSA_redlines_v3.pdf adequately limits operator escalation to timeboxed, auditable sessions. (Action: Rebecca — redline confirmation requested by Thu 10/01)
4) Procurement items: net-60 is acceptable for this deal with reserved capacity; Redwood accepts ACH to acct ending -4321. (Action: David — procurement to circulate PO template once the Order Form line is filled)

We’ll host a 30-minute sync on Tue 09/28 14:00 ET to walk through the redlines and runbook; calendar invite to follow.

Attachments included in this thread: MSA_redlines_v3.pdf (redline w/ comments), operator-runbook-draft.txt (support flows and hash verification steps), order-form-proposed-changes.xlsx (pricing rows highlighted).

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to getting this across the finish line.

Best,

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
